scenes.description: Cold-open hook. Narrator states the past result without yet explaining it. Motif plant: a figure pushing a car uphill — withhold the engine, mirroring the line's own withholding.
scenes.framing: Wide, unhurried — give the line room, no cutting on every phrase.
scenes.shot_intent: Establish the hook without giving away the mechanism — the payoff is withheld on purpose.
scenes.information_role: The viewer learns something changed, not yet what or why.

required_assets.description: motif_hidden_engine_001 (plant) — figure pushing a car uphill, engine not shown/implied hidden. Establishes the visual language this motif will reuse at payoff.

scenes.description: Morning inertia: alarm set early, waking up, the blanket-as-concrete feeling, the to-do list that won't be started.
scenes.framing: Close, tactile — texture of the blanket, weight of the moment
scenes.shot_intent: Make the resistance physically legible — this isn't abstract laziness, it's a felt weight.
scenes.information_role: The viewer recognizes the feeling before the narrator names it.

required_assets.description: Morning bedroom, alarm clock, blanket, unopened to-do list — stock or generated, no faces needed (faceless format).

scenes.description: The self-blaming inner voice: 'I thought I was lazy... push harder, be tougher.'
scenes.overlay_notes: Kinetic typography of the self-talk lines, terse and clipped, not a paragraph block.
scenes.shot_intent: Give the misdiagnosis its own visual beat so the reveal in scene_004 lands as a correction, not a footnote.
scenes.information_role: The viewer sees the narrator's old (wrong) explanation stated plainly.

required_assets.description: Kinetic typography treatment for 'not disciplined enough / push harder / be tougher'.

scenes.description: The correction and the concept: 'wrong fuel' — two types of motivational fuel, extrinsic vs. the still-unnamed second source.
scenes.shot_intent: Introduce the video's central concept as a simple two-tank/two-column diagram, not a data chart — this is the thesis, keep it visually plain so the metaphor (scene_005) carries the weight.
scenes.information_role: The viewer learns the frame: two fuels, one of them is weaker, the narrator had been using it.

required_assets.description: Two-tank or two-column diagram: extrinsic fuel (labeled) vs. second fuel (deliberately left unlabeled/blank — it hasn't been revealed in the source script yet).

scenes.description: Motif payoff: the race car filled with regular gas from the corner store — 'it works, but it's not what the car was built for.' Must visually rhyme with scene_001's motif plant (same car, same visual language).
scenes.shot_intent: This is the video's central visual metaphor — treat it as the hero moment of the extrinsic-motivation explanation.
scenes.information_role: The viewer understands 'extrinsic motivation' as a felt image, not a definition.

required_assets.description: motif_hidden_engine_001 (payoff, partial) — the same race car from scene_001, now shown at a corner-store gas pump being filled with regular gas.

scenes.description: Definition list: extrinsic motivation = money, praise, status, avoiding getting yelled at.
scenes.overlay_notes: Short list reveal, one item at a time, matched to the narrator's own list cadence.
scenes.shot_intent: Ground the metaphor in concrete, recognizable examples before the dopamine explanation.
scenes.information_role: The viewer maps the metaphor onto their own life.

required_assets.description: Sequential text reveal: Money / Praise / Status / Avoiding getting yelled at.

scenes.description: Christmas Eve anticipation vs. Christmas morning anticlimax, mapped onto 'wanting the thing' vs. 'getting the thing.'
scenes.shot_intent: Two-shot contrast: anticipation (warm, lit tree, wrapped presents) cutting to the flatness right after (same room, morning light, presents already open).
scenes.information_role: The viewer feels the anticlimax the narrator is describing, not just hears about it.

required_assets.description: Two-part contrast shot: Christmas Eve anticipation vs. Christmas morning anticlimax, same room.

scenes.description: The promotion-chase / dopamine-crash beat leading into 'chasing the next thing, thinking — okay when I hit this—' where the source script currently cuts off.
scenes.shot_intent: Show the repeating cycle (chase, win, flatten, chase again) as a loop, not a single event — this is what makes the eventual fuel-switch land as a break in the pattern rather than one more win.
scenes.information_role: The viewer sees the treadmill the narrator is stuck on, right before the source material runs out.

required_assets.description: Workplace/desk broll suggesting a repeating cycle — chase, brief high, flatness. PROVISIONAL: this scene's out-point and transition_out depend on the still-missing rest of Phase 2.
